We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong here. Let me start by understanding the situation. My mom used to host Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for all her kids and grandkids for about 50 years. Now she's too old, so we, the four kids, are supposed to take over the tradition by rotating. Each of us has hosted one holiday so far. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family has never been close, and they live all over the country. This year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. At first, it was just a sister trip, but then they invited all their kids and grandkids to meet them there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event, and I agree with that. Plus, I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to figure out what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York and went on about how sad Mom will be that I'm doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't do it because she's renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions and also offered to host the next holiday, which my oldest sister said no to because it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested that me and him could maybe just swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I'm trying to spend time with my wife's family, which is important, especially since they're not as close and live far apart. On the other hand, I'm breaking the tradition that our mom started and that we agreed to continue by rotating. My oldest sister is upset, and I feel like I'm being inconsiderate of her and our mom's wishes. I also tried to offer solutions, like paying for a venue and catering, but she didn't like that idea because it changes the family vibe. I even offered to host the next holiday, but she refused. My brother might be able to help, but it's not certain. I'm feeling stuck because I want to do the right thing, but I also want to spend this special time with my wife's family. Maybe I should think about what's most important here. Is it more important to keep the family tradition alive, or is it more important to spend this time with my wife's family? Both are important, but they seem to be conflicting in this case. I also need to consider how my actions affect my siblings and our mom. She's the one who started this tradition, and she's probably counting on us to keep it going. I wonder if there's a way to compromise. Maybe we could have a smaller gathering at my house and then go to the parade. Or maybe my wife's family could join us for Thanksgiving, but that might not be feasible because they're all going to New York. I'm not sure. I also feel like I'm being inconsiderate by not hosting when it's my turn. My oldest sister is upset, and I can see why. She's probably been looking forward to hosting and has been planning for it all year. By backing out, I'm putting more pressure on her and maybe even on my brother. I guess I need to weigh the importance of spending this time with my wife's family against the importance of keeping our family tradition alive. It's a tough decision, and I'm not sure what the right answer is. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing and not hurting anyone's feelings or breaking a promise to our mom.
